objective: To understand when to keep or drop the e when adding -ous
defs: very brave; willing to face danger
giving a useful benefit or advantage
willing to take risks and try new things

sentences.courageous: The ____________________ firefighter ran into the burning building without a moment's hesitation.
sentences.outrageous: It was ____________________ that someone had eaten the whole birthday cake before the party had even started.
sentences.gorgeous: The view from the hilltop was ____________________, with golden fields stretching as far as the eye could see.
sentences.advantageous: Arriving early was ____________________ because they chose the best seats before the doors opened.
sentences.adventurous: The ____________________ explorer had already visited more than forty countries by the age of thirty.
sentences.marvellous: The magician performed a ____________________ trick that left the entire audience completely speechless.
sentences.famous: The ____________________ artist had painted in a small studio overlooking the sea for most of her life.
sentences.nervous: The ____________________ pupil took a deep breath before walking out onto the stage.
sentences.enormous: An ____________________ hot air balloon drifted slowly over the rooftops on a bright Saturday morning.
sentences.joyous: The ____________________ celebration filled the streets with music, colour and dancing late into the evening.

starter.question: Add -ous to each word. Do you keep or drop the e?
starter.ruleBox: After g or ge, keep the e to preserve the soft /j/ sound: courage → courageous. After most other endings, drop the e: fame → famous.

thisWeeksWordsQ: What do you notice about today's words?
thisWeeksWordsPrompt: Some words keep the e when -ous is added. Can you spot which ones and why?
thisWeeksWordsExplanation: After g or ge, the e is kept to preserve the soft /j/ sound: courage → courageous. In other words the e is dropped: fame → famous, nerve → nervous. The word sort today will help you see this pattern clearly.

clicks.label: Original meaning
clicks.body: having heart; brave in the face of danger

clicks.label: Then
clicks.body: Entered English in the 1300s as courage; courageous formed by adding -ous.

clicks.label: Now
clicks.body: We use courageous to mean very brave or willing to face difficulty.

clicks.label: In today's words
clicks.body: The e stays in courageous because the g must stay soft: corage + ous = courageous.

wordSortQ: Can you sort these words into two groups?

wordSort.box1sub: The e stays to keep the soft /j/ sound
wordSort.box2sub: The e is removed when -ous is added
wordSort.hint: Look at the letter before -ous. Is there a g or ge? If so, the e stays.
wordSort.answerNote: E kept: courageous, outrageous, gorgeous, advantageous. E dropped: adventurous, marvellous, famous, nervous, enormous, joyous.
wordSort.exampleLine: courage + ous = courageous (e kept) | fame + ous = famous (e dropped)

wordShed.def: causing great wonder or admiration; extraordinary
wordShed.sentence: The marvellous acrobat spun three times in the air before landing perfectly on her feet.

morphMatrix.def: the ability to do something difficult despite being afraid
